intro: Professionals and everyday users convert fahrenheit (°F) to celsius (°C) when working across us_customary and si standards in meteorological weather reports, culinary oven calibration, HVAC setpoints, and clinical thermometry. One fahrenheit equals -17.222222 celsius, while 1 celsius equals 33.8 fahrenheit. Whether you are verifying temperature specifications on imported equipment, cross-checking technical datasheets, or scaling practical measurements, this converter applies the exact NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 reference relationship with instant precision.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: Temperature Offset vs. Temperature Interval Trap
items: Converting a specific thermometer reading between Fahrenheit (°F) and Celsius (°C) requires applying the zero-point offset (+32 or +273.15). However, when converting a temperature change or difference (ΔT, such as a 10° rise), you must use only the scale ratio (1 °C = 1.8 °F = 1 K) without adding the offset.
Remember that -40 °C and -40 °F are the exact crossover point where both relative scales read the same value.

faqs.question: How many celsius (°C) are in 1 fahrenheit (°F)?
faqs.answer: There are -17.22222222 celsius (°C) in 1 fahrenheit (°F), which rounds to -17.2222 °C for everyday calculations. Conversely, 1 celsius equals 33.8 fahrenheit.

faqs.question: How do I convert fahrenheit to celsius (°F to °C)?
faqs.answer: To convert fahrenheit to celsius, use the formula: °C = (°F − 32) × 5/9. For example, converting 68 °F gives 20 °C.

faqs.question: What is 68 fahrenheit in celsius?
faqs.answer: 68 fahrenheit (°F) equals exactly 20 celsius (°C) using standard NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 conversion factors.
